standard.title: Manipulate phonemes in words
standard.description: orally manipulate phonemes in spoken words by addition, deletion and substitution of initial, medial and final phonemes to generate new words (phonological awareness)
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can segment words into separate phonemes including consonant blends (AC9E1LY09). They have not yet manipulated individual phonemes by adding, deleting or substituting them to generate new words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students manipulate phonemes in spoken words by addition, deletion and substitution in initial, medial and final positions to generate new words.

nodes.label: Phoneme deletion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can delete a phoneme from a spoken word to produce a new word.
nodes.minimum_width: Delete the initial or final phoneme from at least two words and correctly state the new word formed.
nodes.typical_width: Delete initial, medial and final phonemes from spoken words to produce new words across a range of word patterns.
wider: Delete phonemes from words with consonant blends — e.g. delete the /s/ from 'slip' to get 'lip'
Chain deletions: delete a phoneme, then delete another from the result
nodes.hinge_reason: Phoneme deletion is the foundational manipulation — students who cannot reliably delete cannot perform substitution (N2), which requires deleting and replacing, or addition (N3), which requires inserting into a held phoneme sequence.

response_modes.reason: Phoneme deletion requires secure phoneme segmentation — students who cannot reliably segment cannot reliably delete. Repeated practice, especially at the medial position, builds the precision needed.

success_criteria: Student correctly produces the new word after deleting an initial phoneme
Student correctly produces the new word after deleting a final phoneme

nodes.label: Phoneme substitution
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can substitute an initial, medial or final phoneme in a spoken word to generate a new word.
nodes.minimum_width: Substitute at least one phoneme in a spoken word (at any position) and correctly state the new word.
nodes.typical_width: Substitute initial, medial and final phonemes to generate new words, including substituting medial vowel sounds in CVC words (e.g. pin→pen→pan) and final consonants (e.g. pet→peg).
wider: Build a phoneme substitution chain: change one phoneme at a time across a series of words
Use phoneme substitution to generate rhyme families by substituting initial phonemes
nodes.hinge_reason: Medial vowel substitution specifically — the hardest manipulation — underpins the short and long vowel reading and spelling work in AC9E1LY11; students who cannot substitute medial vowels will struggle to distinguish vowel patterns in words.

response_modes.reason: Medial substitution (changing the vowel) is harder than initial or final substitution because vowel sounds are more abstract. Students need specific practice with medial vowel substitution as a distinct skill, not just more of initial substitution.

success_criteria: Student correctly substitutes an initial phoneme to make a new word
Student correctly substitutes a medial vowel to make a new word (e.g. pin → pen)

nodes.label: Phoneme addition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can add a phoneme to a spoken word in initial, medial or final position to generate a new word.
nodes.minimum_width: Add a phoneme to at least two spoken words (at any position) and correctly state the new word.
nodes.typical_width: Add phonemes to initial, medial and final positions in spoken words to generate new words, including adding phonemes to make consonant blends (e.g. add /s/ to 'lip' to get 'slip').
wider: Explore how adding a final phoneme changes a word family (e.g. 'an' → 'and' → 'hand')
Combine addition and substitution tasks in oral word-play chains
success_criteria: Student correctly adds a phoneme to make a new word
Student states the position (beginning/middle/end) where they added the phoneme
